newsitem.title: USA: N.J. picks Merrill to sell $3.4 bln bonds.
newsitem.headline: N.J. picks Merrill to sell $3.4 bln bonds.

text.p: New Jersey Treasurer Brian Clymer said Tuesday the state has selected Merrill Lynch & Co Inc to be senior manager on a planned $3.4 billion pension obligation bond deal.
The state said Lehman Brothers and Goldman Sachs & Co would act as co-senior managers in the syndicate.
The proposed taxable bond deal would be the largest single sale ever by a municipal bond issuer, although some advisers have suggested the deal may be priced in pieces instead.

Gov Christine Whitman sparked controversy by proposing the massive underwriting, which she said will solve the state's unfunded pension liability problem while at the same time free up more than $600 million for the state budget.

But critics say the proposal rests on risky assumptions that rely on arbitrage earnings between the rate New Jersey will have to pay on the bonds and the rate state investment managers expect to earn on the proceeds.
Other analysts said the size of the issue is also a risk to the state's credit ratings, since it would increase the state's outstanding debt by about 35 percent.
